rubric.criterion: Identifies deployment TaskCancelled consuming the ordinary failure budget on A, B, and C; uses the supplied defer contract for controlled resumable maintenance rather than merely increasing the count or making all failures free.

Stops queue acquisition and handles an acquisition already in flight before quiescing work; readiness alone does not stop this poll loop. Keeps ownership valid while work/checkpointing is active and relinquishes only after safe durable progress or an explicit unresolved failure path.

Preserves stable job identity, confirmed durable cursor and replay safety across replacement processes. Does not claim cancelling the handler completes the job or that a local checkpoint guarantees recovery when its commit is uncertain.

Fits cooperative stopping and confirmed checkpoint/release within the actual 90-second deadline with margin, or explicitly changes the rollout/drain design. Explains why 12–24-hour jobs and twice-daily replacement require resumability or retained draining workers rather than a guaranteed full finish during shutdown.

Specifies the repeated A-to-B-to-C maintenance schedule and asserts eventual completion without consuming the malformed-input failure budget; also checks admission races, crash/kill, and a failed or ambiguous checkpoint rather than testing only a clean SIGTERM.
Leaves supplied files unchanged, performs no live operation, and distinguishes recommendations or unrun checks from observations actually present in the fixture or local commands.
